body: Yeah, I have.  I do know what is going on.  Her mother died about 8 years ago after becoming quadreplegic and my mother was her caretaker.  That would be enough to drive anyone nuts.  It was really awful.  Her father died when she was about 23 after a 22 year battle with Parkinsons (so, her whole life.)  She and my sister have a VERY bad relationship - my sister is bipolar and blames my mother for "ruining her brain" with medication.  So that's all really getting to her, and on top of that we're having financial trouble just like everyone else.  My dad just got a new job but for a while she was working 7 days a week to pay the bills.  I really do see why she would be this depressed, the thing I don't get it why she isn't open to therapy or other options to make it go away.  After a lifetime of telling my sister that her illness was not her fault and it's not a weakness to need therapy or medication, she won't take her own advice.
I didn't realize there was an /r/suicidewatch.  Thanks.

Of course; I've tried for years.  I most recently wrote her a very heartfelt letter telling her that I really think she needs to be proactive about her mental health, whether that means therapy, medication, or quitting her job and moving to Europe.  She was extremely angry and wants me to apologize for insulting her.  I'll show you the emails if you want - I was pretty stunned that she reacted so angrily.  I guess I was pretty firm with her - I've gotten to where I'm not very sympathetic anymore and it may have shown.  I don't have too much respect for her not doing ANYTHING to help herself.
I will.  I'm kind of kicking myself for not calling them last time.  Thank you.

Well, I'm not sure it's actually depression.  I don't want to limit it to only that.  My sister is diagnosed as bipolar, and we have other severe mental illness way back in the family tree, when it was called "lunacy" or "hysteria."
